subject: VIP Suite Docking & Interop — AV/Access Plan
messages:
From: Jordan Reed <jordan.reed@harborevent.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 08:02:00 -0700
Subject: VIP suite — initial docking & AV notes

Hi Marcus,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. I sketched a couple of options for the VIP suite at Harbor Pier (attached: suite_floorplan_v2.pdf). High-level points: 

- Dedicated double-door roll-up for equipment loading (dock D3) — 20 minute load window recommended.
- Primary videoconference bridge will be a managed cloud bridge; we can provision a local failover transcode if you want on-site redundancy.
- Network: two separate public subnets plus a private management VLAN. We can put the bridge on VLAN 200 and guest SSID on VLAN 50.
- Power: two redundant 20A circuits on separate phases near the headwall.
- AV rack space: 6RU reserved; we can provision more for a dedicated transcode box.

Questions for you:
1) Do you want the managed bridge + local transcode fallback, or managed only?
2) How many concurrent camera streams do you expect for the exec suites (primary + overflow)?
3) Are there any vendor insurance or name-on-insurance requirements we should be aware of for on-site integrators?

I can book an AV site visit Thurs afternoon if that works.

Jordan
Jordan Reed
Senior Venue Operations
Harbor Eventworks
Attachment: suite_floorplan_v2.pdf (floorplan, 1.2MB)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Reed <jordan.reed@harborevent.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: VIP suite — initial docking & AV notes

Jordan — thanks, this is helpful. Quick answers inline and a couple follow-ups.

1) Fallback strategy: we prefer managed bridge as primary with a lightweight on-site transcode + N+1 failover. The transcode should only be used when the cloud bridge falls below our latency SLO (150ms median). Local fallback config must be automated.
2) Streams: plan for 3x HD RTSP feeds (primary camera trio) + 2 overflow laptop screens. So assume 5 concurrent encoded outputs, plus one recording stream.
3) Insurance: our legal team will need venue certificate naming Redwood Inference as additional insured for the event day. I'll confirm details and send a template.

Logistics asks: can you reserve dock D3 for a 30-minute window at 07:30 on the day of load-in? We'll be shipping two 19" racks and a flight case. Also, can Harbor confirm a crew parking spot near the loading dock for two vans (license plates to be provided)?

Evelyn, Karthik — tagging you for AV vendor recommendation and our transcode config (we should keep the local fallback under 8RU and prefer NVENC-based boxes). Also, please review the proposed VLAN segmentation — I don't want guest traffic touching the management plane.

If Thursday site visit works, let's do Thu 14:00. Jordan — please confirm and I'll send calendar invites.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Infrastructure Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Reed <jordan.reed@harborevent.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: VIP suite — initial docking & AV notes

Thanks Marcus — all sounds good.

We can hold D3 at 07:30 for 30 minutes; I'll put that in the loading schedule and mark the crew parking. I attached a lightweight bridge_config_template.csv that maps the VLANs and failover priorities we discussed.

On insurance — Harbor can provide the standard exhibitor/additional-insured rider. Please send the Redwood template and I'll get procurement to sign off; turnaround typically 48 hours.

Site visit: Thu 14:00 confirmed. I'll have our AV lead, Cindy Alvarez, on the call and she'll bring a second copy of the rack layout to validate RU counts.

On the transcode box: NVENC is fine — Cindy will propose a 6RU NVENC chassis that does HW transcoding with a passive failover to cloud. If you want, she can scope a small POC during the visit.

Jordan

Attachment: bridge_config_template.csv (CSV, 4KB)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Reed <jordan.reed@harborevent.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 09:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: VIP suite — initial docking & AV notes

Forwarding Jordan's notes with a couple internal action items so we have a single source of truth.

Action items: 
- Marcus: share Redwood insurance template with Jordan by EOD today (I'll follow up with legal).
- Karthik: confirm the exact transcode part numbers we allow (we prefer vendor list A or pre-approved hardware). We need RU, power draw, and a simple rollback plan if the transcode fails.
- Evelyn: book our AV integrator for the site visit Thurs 14:00 (estimate 2 techs, 3 hours on-site). Please include questions about cabling path to the headwall and if an on-site switch with SFP+ uplink will be available.

Notes for the visit: bring a camera feed checklist (3 camera angles + overflow), an inventory of patch panels, and the load-in manifest. Jordan — we'll meet you at the dock at 07:15 on load day to sign in with security.

Laura Bennett
Program Manager, Events
Redwood Inference
